correctness.rationale: For every frozen history, the current choice maximizes a report-separable, supporter-monotone candidate priority: affine residual-budget support in fallback and affordable-first minimum price in the MES phase. A current lie cannot improve a genuinely approved candidate priority or worsen a genuinely disapproved incumbent, hence OSP. An exact earliest-large-payment argument gives wEJR; the cited and inspected Theorem 3.14 of Phillips et al. guarantees inherited wEJR+ under matching normalized MES rules. The standalone verifier passed 66,288 fixed states, 184,734 deletion checks, 1,187,136 OSP comparisons, and 22,894 dynamic histories; no finite test is presented as an infinite proof.

These antecedents are used openly as ingredients, not evaded.

originality.rationale: The proposed nonnegative-weight, report-responsive completion is not a statement in the examined primary sources. The main 2026 source explicitly leaves OSP-preserving completion open. The 2025 Phillips et al. theorem already covers the stronger fairness inheritance and is acknowledged. Actual published-record search and 48 accessible prior claims yielded no equivalent OSP completion; unindexed or later literature remains a priority risk.
residual_risks: Semantic search can miss similarly proved results under other voting-completion terminology.

value.rationale: The motivating 2026 paper identifies preservation of OSP when an early-terminating proportional voting rule is completed as an open design issue. The constructive result gives full voter-responsive outputs at every round while retaining immediate truthfulness and known proportional group guarantees; the monotone separable score invariant explains a general safe family of continuations. Its value is not based on the number of verification tests or a routine numerical improvement.
